channel.title: Use & Like: app news
channel.description: What changed in the apps you use, in our own words, with what it means for you and what to do about it.

item.title: Buy now pay later on Black Friday: fees, interest and credit scores
item.description: Buy now pay later splits a purchase into payments: pay-in-4 plans from PayPal, Afterpay and Affirm charge no interest, monthly plans can cost up to about 36% a year, and whether a plan shows up on your credit report depends on the company.

item.title: Encrypted RCS messaging between iPhone and Android explained
item.description: Texts between iPhones and Android phones can be end-to-end encrypted since Apple and Google started rolling it out in beta on 11 May 2026, but only over RCS, with iOS 26.5 or later, the latest Google Messages and a supported carrier.

item.title: Use old router as access point: how it works and what you lose
item.description: An old router can add Wi-Fi to a weak room as an access point, connected to your main router by cable, while the main router keeps running the network; set up as a second full router, it can break gaming, port forwarding and printer sharing.

item.title: WhatsApp Web: India warns to log out on shared computers
item.description: India's Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) says WhatsApp Web sessions left open on office, cyber café or other shared computers are being used to take over accounts and commit fraud. Closing the browser window doesn't end the session, so the advisory asks users to log out by hand every time.

item.title: 10 new photo and video apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These camera and editing apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Photo & Video charts this week, from film-look cameras and a VHS camcorder to a teleprompter and a RAW editor.

item.title: 10 new productivity apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These productivity apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Productivity charts this week, from a handwriting notebook and a talking keyboard to planners, countdowns and a shift calendar.

item.title: 10 new travel apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These travel apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Travel charts this week, from a gas price finder and Connecticut's mobile ID to translators, cruise port guides and a plane radar.

item.title: 10 new weather apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These weather apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Weather charts this week, from 3D storm radar and hurricane prep to northern lights odds and snow forecasts.

item.title: 5 new lifestyle apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These lifestyle apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's paid Lifestyle chart this week, from a pocket typewriter for letters to a Christmas countdown and a private journal.

item.title: 7 new music apps for iPhone climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These music apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Music charts this week, from record and cassette players for your Apple Music library to a free drum machine and a four-track recorder.

item.title: 7 new utility apps for iPhone climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These utility apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Utilities charts this week, from widgets and a keyboard for the foldable iPhone Duo to Google Wallet's new iPhone app.

item.title: 9 new health and fitness apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These health and fitness apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's paid Health & Fitness charts this week, from a step graph for the Apple Watch and a running app to a newborn log and breathing exercises.

item.title: Apple Wallet Connecticut driver's license and ID coming in 2027
item.description: Connecticut residents will be able to add a driver's license or state ID to Apple Wallet on iPhone and Apple Watch starting in 2027, after the state's governor set a target of August 2027 for Apple, Google and Samsung wallets.

item.title: ChatGPT Edu for University of California students from December
item.description: The University of California is paying OpenAI $1.2 million for one year of ChatGPT Edu for all its students, staff and faculty, starting in December. They also get OpenAI's Codex coding agent.

item.title: ChatGPT new model: GPT-6.2 Sol in Chat, GPT-5.6 Sol retires 23 December
item.description: OpenAI is adding GPT-6.2 Sol to the Chat tab in ChatGPT from 23 November for Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise users, less than a week after it arrived in Work and Codex. The older GPT-5.6 Sol leaves Chat, Work and Codex on 23 December.

item.title: ChatGPT shopping: help page drops 'no partnership influence' line
item.description: OpenAI's help page on shopping in ChatGPT used to say product results were picked independently and not influenced by any OpenAI partnerships; that line is gone. The page now says only that product results aren't ads and explains how products and merchants are picked.

item.title: ChatGPT teen safety: report says 41% of test answers were harmful
item.description: A report from the Center for Countering Digital Harm says ChatGPT's teen accounts gave harmful answers to 41% of 120 test prompts about self-harm, eating disorders and drugs, and to 82% when the testers used simple workarounds. Two of four linked parent accounts got no safety alert.

item.title: Claude Android app redesign moves menus to a bottom bar
item.description: Anthropic is rolling out a new version of its Claude app for Android with a bottom navigation bar and Material 3 Expressive design touches. The side menu stays, but it's now mainly for your chat history.

item.title: ClipReel: AI video editor in your browser that edits by chat
item.description: ClipReel is a new browser video editor where you type the edit you want, such as a trim, captions or a vertical crop, see a preview and then add it to the timeline. You can try it without an account, and paid plans start at $49 a month.

item.title: DualWeather: free weather app shows Celsius and Fahrenheit at once
item.description: DualWeather shows every temperature in Celsius and Fahrenheit side by side, in the app and in its widgets, with your own unit first. It's free with no ads or in-app purchases, and was #28 among free Weather apps on the US App Store on 23 November.

item.title: Duo Paint app: mix real-looking colors and paint on iPhone and iPad
item.description: Duo Paint is a $2.99 painting app for iPhone and iPad where you mix colors in wells, then paint with brushes or a spatula on different surfaces. It was #50 among paid Graphics & Design apps on the US App Store on 23 November.

item.title: Firefox iOS Gecko engine: why Firefox on iPhone still uses WebKit
item.description: Mozilla says Apple's EU rules would make it ship Firefox with its own Gecko engine as a separate new app instead of an update, so iPhone users would have to move bookmarks, passwords and history by hand. For now Firefox on iPhone stays on Apple's WebKit.

item.title: Fitbit vs Google Health app: what changed for Fitbit users in 2026
item.description: In 2026 the Fitbit app became the Google Health app, Fitbit accounts gave way to Google accounts, and from 28 November third-party apps and clock faces can no longer be installed on Fitbit watches.

item.title: Fold Clock turns your iPhone into a bedside clock with sleep sounds
item.description: Fold Clock fills your iPhone or iPad screen with a large clock and plays sleep sounds such as rain, ocean waves or a fan, with a sleep timer, for $1.99 and nothing to buy inside. It was #87 among paid Utilities apps on the US App Store on 23 November.

item.title: Galaxy S27 may get a Dynamic Island-style Now Bar, leak suggests
item.description: Changes spotted by SamMobile in One UI 9.5 suggest the Now Bar's Live Notifications, such as timers and directions, would move from the top-left corner to the top center around the selfie camera, Tech Advisor reports. Samsung hasn't confirmed it.

item.title: GetYourVibeOn syncs Apple Music playlists with Philips Hue scenes
item.description: GetYourVibeOn saves an Apple Music playlist and a lighting scene from Apple Home or Philips Hue together as one "Vibe" that starts with a single tap, for $3.99 on iPhone and iPad. It was #55 among paid Lifestyle apps on the US App Store on 23 November, two days after it came out.

item.title: Google AI Mode adds your Drive files, with Wallet and Gemini chats next
item.description: Personal Intelligence in Google Search's AI Mode can now draw on your Docs, Sheets and PDFs in Google Drive, Google announced on 23 November. Linking your Gemini app chats can be set up now and starts working in the coming weeks, and read-only access to cards in Google Wallet is coming later.

item.title: Google Assistant vs Gemini for Home: what changes on your speakers
item.description: Google Assistant stops working on Google's smart speakers and displays on 2 August 2027 and the Nest app closes on 25 January 2027, so Nest owners move to the Google Home app and Gemini for Home, with some features behind a Home Premium plan from $10 a month.

item.title: Googlebook vs Chromebook: what Google's new laptops mean for you
item.description: Googlebooks are Android-based laptops from $899 that went on sale in October, while existing Chromebooks keep getting updates for their supported lifetime, with ChromeOS patches promised through mid-2034.

item.title: iPhone alarm volume too low? iOS 27 has a separate alarm slider
item.description: iOS 27 lets your iPhone alarm ring at its own volume, separate from your ringtone, so a quiet ringer no longer means a quiet alarm. The setting is off by default, so alarms still follow the ringtone volume until you change it.

item.title: Lufthansa Group app brings six airlines and Miles & More together
item.description: The new Lufthansa Group app lets you book, check in and keep boarding passes for Lufthansa, SWISS, Austrian Airlines, Brussels Airlines, ITA Airways and Discover Airlines in one place. It also shows your Miles & More balance and status, and it's free on the App Store and Google Play from 23 November.

item.title: Marvel Comics app update: iPhone Duo support and screenshots allowed
item.description: The new Marvel Comics app, which launched on 16 November to replace Marvel Unlimited, now fits the foldable iPhone Duo's screen and no longer blocks screenshots and screen recording. Landscape reading on all devices is planned for a later update.

item.title: MUTAVIA II synth app for iPhone and iPad: $7.99 launch price
item.description: MUTAVIA II is a new synthesizer app that keeps changing a sound and its sequence through two linked mutation lanes, with 32 patch sockets and seven memory slots. It costs $7.99 until 6 December, and the price goes up on 7 December.

item.title: Obsidian Grok Bot: xAI's agent can now manage notes in your vault
item.description: Grok Bot, xAI's paid AI agent, can now connect to an Obsidian vault to create, search and manage notes, update links and save things from the web. It can also make Bases and Canvas files, and the changes reach your other devices through Obsidian Sync.

item.title: One UI 9.5 may move the Now Bar around the camera, like the Dynamic Island
item.description: Samsung's live notifications pill, the Now Bar, may move from beside the clock to the middle of the screen, wrapped around the front camera, according to a One UI 9.5 build SamMobile obtained. Samsung hasn't announced it, and it isn't in the current One UI 9.5 beta.

item.title: One UI 9.5 Quick Panel: new search when you edit the buttons
item.description: The One UI 9.5 beta lets you search for a Quick Panel button by app or feature name while you edit the panel, instead of scrolling through the whole list. Samsung didn't list it in the beta's notes; it showed up in a video posted on X by Tarun Vats.

item.title: PhotoSynth photo to music app turns any picture into a song on iPhone
item.description: PhotoSynth turns a photo into a short piece of music: a line sweeps across the picture and plays a melody with chords and bass, in a key and tempo picked from the image. It came out on 21 November for $4.99 and was #97 among paid Music apps on the US App Store on 23 November.

item.title: Samsung AI watermark may get an off switch in One UI 9.5
item.description: Text in the One UI 9.5 beta for the Galaxy S26, found by Android Authority, points to a "Show visible AI watermark" setting that would hide the star badge Galaxy AI adds to edited photos. Samsung hasn't confirmed it will reach the final update.

item.title: Samsung Call Screening may get cloud transcription in One UI 9.5
item.description: Unfinished code in the One UI 9.5 beta, found in an Android Authority teardown, points to an opt-in "Cloud transcription" setting that would send incoming call audio to Samsung's servers for more accurate transcripts. Samsung hasn't announced it, and it can't be turned on yet.

item.title: Samsung Galaxy Watch 2027: no new model, a report says
item.description: Samsung won't release a new Galaxy Watch in 2027 and will move to a new model every other year, according to Korea's ETNews; the next one would come in 2028. Samsung hasn't confirmed it.

item.title: Samsung Gallery can stitch photos together in the One UI 9.5 beta
item.description: Samsung Gallery in the One UI 9.5 beta can now combine photos and screenshots into one picture, side by side or stacked, without cropping them. The option sits in the Collage menu, so you no longer need a separate stitching app.

item.title: SatData: offline compass and GPS app for iPhone that works without signal
item.description: SatData is a 4.99-dollar iPhone app from developer Matthew Avery that shows your position, altitude, heading and sun and moon times with no mobile signal, explained in plain words. It was #37 in Navigation on the US App Store's paid chart on 23 November.

item.title: Save emails as PDF on iPhone and Mac with the new Archivia Mail app
item.description: Archivia Mail turns your emails into PDF files, with attachments and the original messages, in folders on your iPhone, iPad or Mac, then can free up space on the mail server once it has checked every copy. It costs $1 once and was #82 among paid Productivity apps on the US App Store on 23 November.

item.title: Tapko Octaver guitar octave app turns your guitar into bass on iPhone
item.description: Tapko Octaver shifts a guitar signal one octave down into bass range, for single-note bass lines and riffs, for $2.99 on iPhone and iPad. It came out on 23 November and was #41 among paid Music apps on the US App Store that day.

item.title: TETSUO app: a $3.99 drum synth for iPhone and iPad with no samples
item.description: TETSUO builds every drum sound from one synthesized voice instead of samples, with a filter, bitcrusher and waveshaper to push it, and records knob settings into up to eight sections that play back in a loop. It was #85 among paid Music apps on the US App Store on 23 November.

item.title: Threads iPad app is coming soon, built for the bigger screen
item.description: Threads head of design Christopher Clare shared a first look at an iPad app on 23 November and said it is coming very soon, designed for the larger display rather than a stretched iPhone app. Meta hasn't given a date.

item.title: Tiny Computers app: ten retro computers you can type on, on iPhone
item.description: Tiny Computers is a 3.99-dollar app with ten miniature retro computers, each with a working screen and keyboard, where you can type commands, draw in paint programs and play desktop games. It was #1 among paid Entertainment apps on the US App Store on 23 November.

item.title: Tiny Steps baby milestone app: a guide from birth to age five
item.description: Tiny Steps: Milestone Guide is a new $1.99 baby milestone app for iPhone and iPad that explains child development from birth to age five, with play ideas for each age. It was #46 among paid Education apps on the US App Store on 23 November.

item.title: Typefully now lets you add up to 20 photos and videos to an X post
item.description: The post scheduler Typefully raised its limit for a single X post from four to 20 photos, videos and GIFs, and teams can now schedule quotes of a post before the original goes out. Typefully added both on 18 November.

item.title: Uber recording rides: Recorded Rides pilot films the whole trip in 4 US cities
item.description: Uber is testing Recorded Rides, trips where the driver's phone films the whole drive with its front camera. The US pilot runs in Baltimore, Raleigh, Indianapolis and St. Louis.
